title: German Transport Minister Backs Tesla FSD in EU, Floats National Path
key_facts: Transport Minister Steffen Bilger (CDU) said at a Tagesspiegel Background conference in Berlin that he wants Tesla’s FSD (Supervised) used across the EU in good time, per dpa.
If no EU agreement is reached, one must discuss what can be done in Germany.
He acknowledged open technical and unresolved liability issues but put innovation and possible safety gains first.
Dutch regulator RDW granted a provisional approval on 10 April 2026 that applies only in the Netherlands unless other states adopt it.
By end of September Lithuania, Estonia, Denmark, Belgium, Slovenia and the Czech Republic had adopted it; Germany, France, Italy and Spain had not.
EU-wide approval needs a qualified majority (15 of 27 states, 65 percent of population); the 6 Oct committee agenda only continued discussion, so a decision is likely not before December.
quote_evidence: Federal Transport Minister Steffen Bilger (CDU) wants to advocate for Tesla’s driver assistance system “Full Self-Driving (Supervised)” to be used throughout the EU in a timely manner.
However, the draft agenda for the TCMV meeting on October 6 only provided for a continuation of the discussion, not a vote.
why_it_matters_hint: Germany, the EU’s largest market, is leaning toward Tesla’s system while approval stays unsettled.
